steps.title: Listen to four pieces of advice from a doctor and a chemist.
steps.sub: Notice the form each one uses.

items.text: You could try this cream, which should help.
It’s a good idea to keep your windows closed at night.
I don’t think you should feel bad.

steps.title: Look at the last sentence again.
steps.sub: I don’t think you should feel bad.
steps.prompt: Why doesn’t the speaker say “I think you shouldn’t feel bad”?
options: In English the negative usually moves to the first verb: I don’t think you should …
Because shouldn’t does not exist at all in modern spoken English.
Because the speaker is a doctor, and doctors always speak more formally.
steps.answer: In English the negative usually moves to the first verb: I don’t think you should …
steps.why: I don’t think you should is the natural form. I think you shouldn’t is possible but sounds much stronger.

steps.title: Asking for and giving advice
steps.html:
What you are doingWhat you say
asking for adviceWhat should I do? / Have you got any advice? / What would you do?
giving normal adviceYou should take it easy. / You ought to see a doctor.
a softer suggestionYou could try this cream. / Why don’t you talk to her?
a general good ideaIt’s a good idea to keep the windows closed.
advising againstI don’t think you should lift anything heavy.
a strong rule, not adviceYou mustn’t lift anything heavy. / He must keep still.
putting yourself in their placeIf I were you, I’d see a doctor.

Should and could are followed by the base form: you should take, never should to take.

Ought to means the same as should, but it keeps the to: You ought to see a doctor.

Why don’t you …? is a question in form but advice in meaning: Why don’t you take a break?

Should is advice; must and mustn’t are rules. A doctor says you should rest but you mustn’t lift anything heavy.

If I were you, I’d … is a second conditional. That is the grammar of Unit 11, Lesson 31.

steps.title: Choose the best advice.
steps.prompt: “I can’t sleep at the moment.”
options: You should try to drink less coffee.
You must sleep for eight hours tonight.
You will sleep better if you say so.
steps.answer: You should try to drink less coffee.

steps.title: Choose the best advice.
steps.prompt: “I’ve hurt my back lifting suitcases.”
options: You should take it easy, and you mustn’t lift anything heavy.
You should lift more suitcases to make your back stronger.

steps.title: Covering letter · model
steps.html:
A formal covering letter for a job application. You will write your own at the end.

Application for the position of junior logistics assistant

Aigerim Sarsenova
12 Abay Street, Karaganda
a.sarsenova@mail.com · +7 701 000 00 00

The Recruitment Team
Northline Logistics
4 March

Dear Sir or Madam,

I am writing to apply for the position of junior logistics assistant, advertised on your website on 1 March (vacancy reference NL-114).

I am currently finishing a diploma in transport management at Karaganda Technical College, and I will graduate in June. During my studies I have worked part-time in a warehouse, where I was responsible for checking deliveries and keeping the daily records. That job taught me that a small mistake at eight in the morning becomes a large one by the afternoon.

I am applying to Northline because your company works across five regions and I would like to learn how a large network is organized. As soon as I finish my assignment in May, I will be available full-time.

I attach my CV and the contact details of two referees. I am available for interview at any time.

I look forward to hearing from you.

Yours faithfully,
Aigerim Sarsenova

steps.title: Useful language
steps.sub: The first group is for advice. The second is for the letter.

items.text: I am writing to apply for the position of …
I attach my CV. I am available for interview.
I look forward to hearing from you.

steps.title: Write a covering letter for a job you would like.
steps.sub: About 120–150 words. Follow the five paragraphs of the model.
steps.html:
1. Plan (from the model): 1 which job and where you saw it → 2 your studies and experience → 3 why this company → 4 what you attach and when you are available → 5 the closing line and sign-off.
  • Dear Sir or Madam,
  • I am writing to apply for the position of …
  • I am currently … During my studies I have …
  • I am applying to … because …
  • I attach my CV … I am available for interview.
  • I look forward to hearing from you.
  • Yours faithfully,
I am writing to apply forthe position ofadvertised on your websiteI am currentlyDuring my studiesI was responsible forI attach my CVtwo refereesI am available for interviewI look forward to hearing from youYours faithfully
steps.modelHtml:
• I began with Dear Sir or Madam and ended with Yours faithfully.
  • The first line says which job and where I saw it.
  • I gave one piece of real experience, not only my studies.
  • I said why I am applying to that company.
  • I used no informal phrases anywhere in the letter.
